title: API latency investigation (EN, large http logs, N+1 root cause + caching decision)

content.text: Customers are complaining the dashboard got slow this week. Our SLO is p95 under 800ms on /api/threads and monitoring shows we are way over. Find out what happened and fix it.

Route /api/threads, 14-day percentiles by day: stable p95 ~410-460ms until 2026-08-03, then a step to p95 1840ms / p99 4100ms starting 2026-08-04 ~14:00 UTC. p50 only moved from 120ms to 190ms — the tail exploded, not the median. Deploy marker at 2026-08-04 13:41 UTC: release v5.2.0.

Raw access log sample around the step:

The step coincides exactly with the v5.2.0 deploy (2026-08-04 13:41 UTC): p95 jumped from ~440ms to 1840ms while p50 barely moved — classic per-item amplification for users with many items. v5.2.0 shipped the "unread counts per thread" feature. Checking the query log for amplification.

input.query: SELECT query_fingerprint, calls, mean_ms, calls_per_request FROM query_stats WHERE window='24h' ORDER BY calls DESC LIMIT 20

content.text:
Top fingerprint: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE thread_id = ? AND read_at IS NULL — 4.1M calls/24h, mean 3.8ms, avg 74 calls per /api/threads request. Second: SELECT * FROM threads WHERE user_id = ? — 55k calls, 12ms. The count query did not exist before 2026-08-04.

Full stats:

Confirmed N+1: getThreadList in v5.2.0 issues one unread-COUNT per thread — 74 per request on average, 3.8ms each ≈ 280ms serial DB time on the p50 user, and users with 300+ threads hit multi-second tails. The offender is src/api/threads/list.ts, the per-thread loop added in PR #471.

Fix options:
(a) Batch the counts into ONE grouped query: SELECT thread_id, COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE thread_id IN (…) AND read_at IS NULL GROUP BY thread_id. Cuts 74 round-trips to 1. Estimated p95 back under 600ms.
(b) Additionally cache the unread map per user with a short TTL, invalidated on message-read events.

I recommend shipping (a) immediately — it is a pure query restructure, no semantics change — and doing (b) only if the numbers still miss the SLO: cache invalidation on read-receipts has real edge cases (multi-device) and should not ride an incident fix.
Agreed, (a) now, (b) only if needed and then properly. Ship it behind our normal canary flow please.

Canary deployed (PR #482, branch fix/threads-unread-batch, image sha256:c41d88). 10% traffic for 2h. Canary metrics: p95 388ms, p99 720ms, error rate 0.01% (baseline 0.02%). Query fingerprint count-per-request dropped from 74 to 1. No regression on write paths.

Canary access log:

Canary numbers are decisive: p95 388ms (SLO 800ms, pre-incident baseline ~440ms — we are now FASTER than before the incident, because the old code had a milder per-thread pattern too), p99 720ms, errors at baseline, and the count query collapsed from 74 calls per request to 1. Promoting to 100% and closing out.
Promoted to 100% at 2026-08-07 09:12 UTC as v5.2.1. Post-promotion 6h: p95 holding 390-420ms across all pods.

Done and stable. Wrap-up:
- Root cause: PR #471 (v5.2.0) introduced a per-thread unread COUNT in getThreadList (src/api/threads/list.ts) — an N+1 with avg 74 queries per request; p95 went 440ms → 1840ms.
- Fix: single grouped count query, shipped as PR #482 → v5.2.1, promoted 2026-08-07 09:12 UTC. p95 now 390-420ms, inside the 800ms SLO with margin.
- Deliberately NOT done: the per-user unread cache (option b) — deferred unless numbers regress; multi-device invalidation needs its own design.
- Open follow-ups: (1) add a query-amplification check to CI (fail a PR that raises calls-per-request on hot routes above a threshold — this exact class would have been caught); (2) a short incident note for the customer-facing status page; (3) watch the p95 dashboard for a week — alert threshold temporarily tightened to 600ms.
- For the SLO report: incident window 2026-08-04 14:00 UTC to 2026-08-07 09:12 UTC.
Great work. Write the CI check as a proper ticket with the threshold proposal, and send me the status-page draft before it goes out.

Both underway: ticket PERF-233 created — "CI guard: query calls-per-request budget on hot routes", proposal: fail if a PR raises the per-request query count of any top-10 route by more than 3x, measured on the seeded test dataset. Status-page draft comes to you for approval before publication — nothing goes out without your sign-off. The tightened 600ms alert stays until 2026-08-14, then back to the standard SLO alerting.

rubric: States the root cause: the v5.2.0 unread-counts feature (PR #471) added an N+1 per-thread COUNT in getThreadList (src/api/threads/list.ts), ~74 queries per request.
Preserves the impact numbers: p95 stepped from ~440ms to 1840ms starting 2026-08-04, tail-only (p50 barely moved).
Records the fix decision: batch into one grouped count query — and that the per-user cache (option b) was deliberately deferred with the multi-device invalidation reasoning.
Preserves the fix path: PR #482 / branch fix/threads-unread-batch, canaried at 10%, then promoted as v5.2.1 on 2026-08-07 09:12 UTC.
Preserves the outcome numbers: canary p95 388ms, post-promotion 390-420ms, inside the 800ms SLO.
Keeps the follow-up ticket PERF-233 (CI query-amplification guard) with its 3x threshold proposal.
Keeps the approval gate: the status-page draft goes to the user before publication.
Preserves the temporary monitoring state: alert threshold tightened to 600ms until 2026-08-14, and the incident window recorded for the SLO report.
